Admissions index 0 (feature-on run) and index 5 (feature-off run) record identical fixture operands - snapshot index 6 with configuration {A,B,C}, the committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E}, stored commit index 8 covering it - and both runs had the same first life with the feature enabled, so the persisted commit index exists in both. In the partition, the feature-on run elects A in the two-voter partition (index 2, violated) while the control elects no leader there (index 7, holds) and has exactly one leader overall (index 7, holds). In the control run the restarted node still gets a snapshot install during the repair phase, so the repair phase is not specific to the defect.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, NewRaft cannot return when the replay must hand more batches to fsmMutateCh than that channel's 128-slot buffer holds, because the only consumer of the channel is runFSM, which NewRaft starts after the replay returns; the number of batches is ceil(committed-but-unapplied entries / MaxAppendEntries), so 129 entries above the last applied index stall the constructor with MaxAppendEntries 1 and 8193 entries do so with the default 64. knowledge.statement: On a follower that receives an InstallSnapshot, the handler streams and finalises the snapshot, restores the FSM through fsmMutateCh, sets lastApplied and the last snapshot to the request's last log index and term, and replaces the latest and committed configuration from the request; the local log is then either removed entirely (monotonic stores) or compacted up to the snapshot index. A follower that has fallen behind a leader whose log was compacted is therefore sent a snapshot and ends up with the leader's FSM state, entry suffix and configuration, replacing any divergent entry it held at an index the leader also used.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

interpretations.rationale: Question: can NewRaft fail to return when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs has to replay more committed entries than the FSM mutation channel can hold in batches before runFSM is started? The account is a sourced mechanism plus one retained receipt that could not decide it. Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs runs before the background goroutines and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-754); processLogs batches entries by MaxAppendEntries (raft.go 1320, 1345) and hands each batch to fsmMutateCh, which NewRaft creates with a 128-slot buffer (api.go 560), while the only consumer of that channel is runFSM, started only after NewRaft finishes the replay and the configuration scan (api.go 600-640). If the replay needs more than 128 batches, the constructor blocks on a send that nothing can receive, so it cannot return under those conditions; with MaxAppendEntries=1 that is 129 entries above the last applied index, and with the default 64 it is 8193 entries. Receipt 2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b holds the fixture operands (index 0: 9000 entries above the snapshot, commit index 10000, 141 batches required; index 2: the same for the feature-on mode) and two results, but the construct events (indices 1 and 3) omitted local_id, so no admission could be matched to a result and all three comparisons were recorded unknown. The raw operands of that receipt (index 3 records newraft_returned false while index 1 records true with lastApplied 1000) are retained but not evaluated, so this account claims nothing from them. A successor experiment with the identity field repaired and a 200-entry MaxAppendEntries=1 mode is filed. Premises still to be established: the restart-shaped fixture is supplied by the harness rather than produced by a live node, and reachability of a gap of 129 or 8193 unapplied committed entries under permitted configuration (SnapshotThreshold and MaxAppendEntries are both configurable) is argued from source rather than observed. A local variant with LogNoop entries returned in both modes because prepareLog never sends no-ops to the FSM, which is why the fixture uses LogCommand entries and why the feature-off control is required to exclude a slow fixture.
counterevidence: With RestoreCommittedLogs disabled on the identical fixture the constructor returns with lastApplied still at the snapshot index, so the fixture's size alone does not explain a stall.
A fixture whose entries are no-ops returns in both modes, which shows the stall requires entries that reach the FSM commit path and keeps the question scoped to that path.
limitations: The fixture is supplied by the harness; no live node produced the committed-but-unapplied gap.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate is that construction returns within the observation window; it is contradicted in both feature-on cases and satisfied in both controls. Admission index 2 requires 141 batches (9000 committed entries above the snapshot at MaxAppendEntries 64) and the corresponding construct event at index 3 records newraft_returned false after the 5s window; admission index 6 requires 200 batches from only 200 entries above the snapshot at MaxAppendEntries 1 and its construct event at index 7 also records newraft_returned false. The controls at the same scales (admissions 0 and 4, construct events 1 and 5) return with lastApplied 1000, i.e. still at the snapshot index, and index 1 reports the observed channel capacity 128 with an empty queue, so fixture size, store speed and FSM speed do not explain the difference. Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-754) before NewRaft starts any background goroutine (api.go 600-640); processLogs batches committed entries by MaxAppendEntries (raft.go 1320, 1345) and sends each batch to fsmMutateCh, whose buffer NewRaft creates with 128 slots (api.go 560); the only consumer is runFSM, started after the constructor finishes, so once the buffer is full the send can never complete and NewRaft cannot return. Bounds: the fixture is supplied by the harness rather than produced by a live node, the stalled constructor is abandoned rather than resumed, the observation window is 5s while the source argument (no consumer exists before NewRaft returns) explains why it cannot return later, and only in-memory stores were used. Reachability under permitted configuration is argued rather than observed in a cluster: MaxAppendEntries is configurable from 1 (ValidateConfig allows it; the small-batch case shows 200 entries suffice) and a larger gap follows from a delayed snapshot.
counterevidence: With the feature off, the identical fixtures construct normally, so the fixture's size alone does not explain the stall.
A fixture of no-op entries constructs in both modes because prepareLog never sends no-ops to the FSM, so the stall is specific to entries on the FSM commit path.
